title: Constructible exceptional Frobenius mate, lifted adjunction and comparisons
statement:
Fix primes $p\ne\ell$, $a\ge1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, an algebraic closure $k$ of $k_0$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ in a fixed algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, and $\Lambda\in\{E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. For a finite-type $k_0$-scheme $T_0$ put $T=T_0\times_{k_0}k$, $g_T=\operatorname{id}_{T_0}\times\operatorname{Spec}(\operatorname{Frob}_q)$ with geometric Frobenius, and $P_T=Lg_T^*$ [def-weil-frobenius-detailed, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Use the rational/common-stage bounded constructible categories and Weil pairs $(K,\theta_K:P_TK\xrightarrow{\sim}K)$, whose arrows satisfy $u\theta_K=\theta_LP_T(u)$ [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex]. Let $f_0:X_0\to Y_0$ be a separated finite-type morphism of finite-type $k_0$-schemes, and put $f=f_0\times_{k_0}k:X\to Y$. Use the constructible adjunction $F=Rf_!\dashv G=Rf^!$ on $D^b_c$, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$, for every such $f$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Put $S=P_X$, $T=P_Y$, and assume their exact equivalences with inverse Frobenius transport and the canonical compact-support exchange isomorphism $a:TF\simeq FS$ of [def-exchange-projection], including its rational/common-stage construction. Give $F$ its Weil structure $F(\theta_K)a_K$. Then the adjunction mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]
$$ b:SG\xrightarrow{\eta SG}GFSG\xrightarrow{Ga^{-1}G}GTFG\xrightarrow{GT\varepsilon}GT $$
is an isomorphism, and $(L,\theta_L)\mapsto(GL,G(\theta_L)b_L)$, with arrow $G(u)$, defines a Weil lift of this same constructible $G$. Its unit and counit are Weil morphisms and satisfy the adjunction triangle identities after forgetting. More explicitly the mate obeys
$$ (Ga)(bF)(S\eta)=\eta S,\qquad (\varepsilon T)(Fb)(aG)=T\varepsilon, $$
and the induced structures obey
$$ \theta_{GFK}S(\eta_K)=\eta_K\theta_K,\qquad \varepsilon_L\theta_{FGL}=\theta_LT(\varepsilon_L). $$

On their stated constructible domains, use the standard Frobenius lifts of pullback, direct images, tensor and internal Hom, and the canonical comparisons of [def-exchange-projection]. Composition comparisons, exchange transformations, tensor evaluation, ordinary adjunction maps and the projection transformation are Weil morphisms. Composition, whiskering by these lifted functors and inversion of isomorphisms preserve the Weil-morphism equations. The unit–map–counit mate of any such comparison under the lifted exceptional adjunction is again equivariant; the mate-pasting identities identify these maps with the specified exceptional composition/exchange maps. Thus every such comparison already known to be invertible is an isomorphism of Weil pairs on exactly its proved domain. In the Frobenius square $a=\operatorname{Ex}_!$ is invertible also when the base is non-separated, after rationalization and in the common-stage category. No ambient exceptional right adjoint or separatedness of $X_0,Y_0$ is assumed. Equivariance alone makes no new comparison invertible.

source.place: Proof sentence 1: exceptional adjunction, its unit/counit, comparison maps and mate pasting; returned proof Steps 3–4 and 6.

proof.text: By [lem-pod-weil-frobenius-compact-support-exchange], the specified $a$ is invertible also on non-separated bases and at both field stages. For the assumed constructible $F\dashv G$, [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] identifies the displayed $b$ with the mate of $a^{-1}$. Apply [lem-weil-mate-iso-along-equivalences] with both adjunctions $F\dashv G$ and sides $S,T$; $S$ is an equivalence and $T$ fully faithful, so $b$ is invertible. The Lean proof of adjunction_coherent constructs the mate with asIso and uses the existing generic equivalence/fully-faithful criterion. The specified left comparison is already an isomorphism in its input; no geometric exchange is needed for this abstract clause.

source.place: Proof sentence 1; assembly of returned steps 1–2.

proof.text: The unit formula [lem-pur-mate-unit-compatibility] gives $b_FS\eta=Ga^{-1}\eta S$; cancel $Ga^{-1}$ to get the asserted unit equation. The transpose formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] gives $\varepsilon T\,Fb=T\varepsilon\,a^{-1}G$; cancel $a^{-1}G$ for the counit equation. Apply [lem-sf-fixed-pair-adjunction-lift] to this invertible mate: the lifts use exactly $F\theta\,a$ and $G\theta\,b$, with the original unit, counit and triangles. Its Weil-morphism equations are precisely the two displayed structure equations. The covariant lift specification follows directly from the object/structure formulas of IsoAlgebra.mapOfNatIso and the structure equation of its mapped morphism, without using the unfinished covariant-field-operation-lift theorem.

source.place: Proof sentence 1; assembly of returned steps 3–6.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-frobenius-pullback-monoidal-adjunction-coherence] to the ordinary adjunction, pullback composition and tensor comparisons, and [lem-pod-semilinear-exchange-cube-coherence] to direct-image compositions and exchange cubes. Their comparison equations, followed by naturality at the input Weil structures, give the stated Weil morphisms. The latter node includes semilinear relabeling and refinement independence, so no separatedness of the bases is added.

source.place: Proof sentence 1; assembly of returned steps 8–11.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pod-frobenius-evaluation-projection-coherence] using Step 3's ordinary and tensor maps. It gives the evaluation equation, the open projection square on strict systems and its supplied realizations, and hence equivariance of the actual projection composite on its original domain.

source.place: Proof sentence 1; assembly of returned steps 12–13.

proof.text: For Weil arrows, $(vu)\theta=v\theta'P(u)=\theta''P(vu)$. Multiplying $u\theta=\theta'P(u)$ by inverses gives the equation for $u^{-1}$. Naturality of each lifted functor's comparison gives the equation for its image. These identities give composition, both whiskerings and inverse closure directly from [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex].

source.place: Proof sentence 1; assembly of returned steps 7.

proof.text: Use [lem-pod-equivariant-mates-coefficient-transport] with the lifted exceptional adjunction of Step 2 and the comparisons of Steps 3–4. Its three-factor mate and pasting equalities identify the specified exceptional maps. Its coefficient-transport hypotheses are the supplied data of [def-exchange-projection] (rationalized integral maps; scalar-extension comparisons intertwining units, counits and comparisons, identities for identity extensions, with the tower cocycle) and the common-stage operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]; so the clause applies on rational/common stages, including Weil maps without invariant lattices. Its inverse clause makes exactly the already invertible comparisons isomorphisms of Weil pairs.

source.place: Proof sentence 1; assembly of returned steps 14–15.

proof.text: For the Hom-first evaluation clauses, use the normalized rational evaluation naturality lemma and the common-stage counterpart [lem-pod-normalized-common-evaluation-naturality]. For a Weil pair (M,N), let Q=(M,N), R=(PM,PN) and f=(theta_M inverse op,theta_N):R→Q. Naturality says T(Hf,1) ev_Q = T(1,theta_M inverse) ev_R theta_N. Precompose by T(1,theta_M) and use the inverse equation to obtain T(Hf,theta_M) ev_Q = ev_R theta_N. Insert the canonical Hom comparison and tensor comparison and apply the Hom-first evaluation law from lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation. Both the comparison and H(f) are invertible, which also proves the internal-Hom structure is invertible. The existing normalizations hP,hT,hH,hSC,hκ,hμ identify this calculation with exactly the two EvaluationEquivariant predicates.

source.place: Evaluation paragraph; common-stage evaluation descent, steps 15--16 of lem-pod-derived-automorphism-hom-evaluation.

proof.text: For frobenius_exchanges_isIso, work with the literal whole-system recipe. Pullback along a scheme isomorphism is an equivalence: the functor for its inverse and the system composition/unit isomorphisms provide an equivalence. Thus the generic mate-along-equivalences criterion makes systemExchange invertible. Whisker it by the open extension and compose with the isomorphic systemOpenExchange to get systemCompactExchange. The named compactAlpha_isIso theorem and the explicit inverse-isomorphism factors of compactBeta make compactIntegralAmbient invertible. Reflect this through the full-subcategory inclusion to obtain compactIntegral. The components of localizedTransformation are images under scalar localization, so they remain invertible; the two endpoint equality isomorphisms give modelRationalExchange. Finally isIso_descNatTrans gives the common-stage exchange from these finite-stage isomorphisms. Specialize to the geometric compactification and its three geometric Frobenius automorphisms. This uses no separatedness of the base schemes.
